tier_reason: Independent measurement by the OpenCV project (wiki page last edited 2018-06-22) comparing GStreamer gst-vaapi and gst-libav pipelines against OpenCV's FFmpeg backend; the benchmark code is public (samples/cpp/gstreamer_pipeline.cpp at OpenCV tag 3.4.3, renamed samples/cpp/videocapture_gstreamer_pipeline.cpp in November 2018) and the CPU is stated (Core i5-6600, HD Graphics 530), but no compiler, flags, encoder settings, library versions or run counts are given, so it is not A.

corrections.workload: OpenCV benchmark sample (samples/cpp/gstreamer_pipeline.cpp, now samples/cpp/videocapture_gstreamer_pipeline.cpp). Decode: frames per second of grab+retrieve to BGR over a full-HD 1920x1080 clip encoded with ffmpeg default settings, in mkv, mp4 and avi containers (mpeg2, h264, h265, vp8). Encode: 1000 frames from a synthetic GStreamer videotestsrc SMPTE colour-bar source (resolution set by -r, default 720p; the page does not say which was used), timing only the VideoWriter write call. GStreamer pipelines (gst-vaapi on the Intel iGPU, gst-libav on the CPU) versus OpenCV's FFmpeg backend (CPU software codecs).
corrections.compiler_and_flags: OpenCV built with cmake -DBUILD_EXAMPLES=ON -DWITH_GSTREAMER=ON -DWITH_FFMPEG=ON, make -j8 (build type not given); GStreamer, gstreamer1.0-vaapi, gstreamer1.0-libav and libavcodec are unversioned Ubuntu 17.10 apt packages per the page's install commands; compiler, optimisation flags, encoder settings and OpenCV/GStreamer/FFmpeg versions not stated
corrections.caveats: The win is hardware versus software: gst-vaapi drives the Skylake iGPU's fixed-function codecs, while OpenCV's FFmpeg wrapper had no hardware acceleration at the time (the page says so), so FFmpeg itself, which also supports VA-API, was not measured with hardware decode or encode; this is not GStreamer's own code being faster. Encoders differ (VA-API defaults versus libx264/libvpx defaults through OpenCV's FFmpeg writer), so output quality and bitrate are not equal. Encode input is a synthetic SMPTE colour-bar pattern (default 720p in the sample), not the 1080p clip, and the page does not state the encode resolution. The encode timer covers only the write call: GStreamer's appsrc (block=1) encodes in its own streaming thread, so encoding that overlaps the untimed synthetic-frame grab is hidden, a modest bias in GStreamer's favour; frames still queued at end of stream are not timed. The page's x multipliers are relative to the faster CPU column (gst-libav or FFmpeg), e.g. mp4/mpeg2 decode x1.06 is versus gst-libav 343 fps; versus FFmpeg 258 fps it is x1.41 (derived from page data). gst-vaapi decode was slower than FFmpeg for every mkv input (h264 59 vs 158, h265 65 vs 255, vp8 68 vs 309 fps) and CPU gst-libav lost to FFmpeg on h264, h265 and vp8 decode and on mpeg2 encode (81 vs 106 fps). Single undated-run results from 2018 on Ubuntu 17.10; no run counts or variance. The measured component, gstreamer-vaapi, is no longer in the GStreamer monorepo's main branch (subprojects/ has no gstreamer-vaapi; upstream replaced it with the va plugin in gst-plugins-bad according to forum and distro-packaging search snippets, and this page did not measure that plugin). The benchmark sample linked from the page 404s at master because it was renamed; it is reachable at OpenCV tag 3.4.3 (samples/cpp/gstreamer_pipeline.cpp) and as samples/cpp/videocapture_gstreamer_pipeline.cpp on 4.x. The GitHub repo is a read-only mirror of gitlab.freedesktop.org/gstreamer/gstreamer and carries no benchmarks itself. LICENSE file is LGPL v2.1 text; SPDX LGPL-2.1-or-later per GStreamer's source headers convention, not checked file by file.

notes: Every number in claimed_speedup matches the OpenCV wiki tables (encode h264 193/194/185 vs 51/51/50, vp8 124 vs 12, mpeg2 124 vs 106; decode mp4/h264 376 vs 169, avi/h264 373 vs 159, mp4/h265 391 vs 256, mp4/mpeg2 364 vs 258). Shortcomings to record: hardware iGPU versus CPU software codecs (FFmpeg's own VA-API path not used), unequal encoder settings, synthetic 720p-default encode input not the 1080p clip, write-only encode timer favouring GStreamer's async pipeline, mkv decode much slower with gst-vaapi, 2018 Ubuntu 17.10 run with no versions or flags, and gstreamer-vaapi since removed from GStreamer main in favour of the va plugin. Metadata checked: 3.3k stars, 774 forks, mirror (not a fork), last commit 2026-10-11, LGPL-2.1 LICENSE.
